approach.expect: From the Mount Baker Ranger District office in Sedro-Woolley, drive north on WA-9 to Acme, turn right (east) on Mosquito Lake Road for about 9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River, and continue onto Forest Road 38 for roughly 11 miles to the Elbow Lake Trail's north trailhead (a separate trailhead from 'Pioneer Camp,' which is actually on the trail's south end via Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12). From there, follow Elbow Lake Trail #697 across the Middle Fork Nooksack and up to a switchback near Hildebrand Creek, then pick up the unmaintained Green Creek climbers' path into the Green Creek Cirque beneath Skookum's north/east flank before gaining the ridge. As of mid-2026 this whole approach is compromised: FSR 38 was damaged in the December 2025 floods with no published repair date, and the unofficial log crossing with rope handrails over the Middle Fork Nooksack near the trailhead was also washed out — confirm current conditions with the Mount Baker Ranger District before driving in.

approach.expect: The X Couloir is approached from the south via the Middle Fork Nooksack River Road (FR-38), not from Heliotrope Ridge (that trailhead serves Lincoln's separate NW Face/Wilkes-Booth line). Drive FR-38 toward its mile-12.5 switchback and start hiking/bushwhacking the old decommissioned road around Pt. 4481 toward Rankin Creek — snow travel (often by bike or snowshoe on the lower stretch) leads past East Rankin Lake (~5,120 ft) and up into the basin to a sheltered camp at treeline around 6,100 ft, near the highest trees in the basin below Seward Peak. From camp, an alpine start gets the team into the southwest basin and across the bergschrund crux while it's still cold and firm, climbing roughly 1,500 ft of 30-40° snow and a steep serac step in the X Couloir to the 9,085 ft summit. Total approach is on the order of 7 miles and 3,350 ft of gain to the basin camp. IMPORTANT — access note: as of mid-2026, FR-38 (Middle Fork Nooksack River Road) is closed at milepost 7 by a washout from the December 2025 floods, with no confirmed repair timeline, and a separate seasonal gate at Wallace Creek (~mile 10) closes the road December 1-June 15 for elk calving; confirm current road status with the Mount Baker Ranger District (Glacier Public Service Center) before a trip, since the drivable road-end — and therefore the length of the approach — varies year to year.

approach.expect: From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS 39); turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37). FS 37 normally continues 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide Trailhead. When open, hike Skyline Divide Trail #678 through old-growth forest switchbacks and into meadows on the ridge crest (~2 mi), follow the crest to the trail's high point (~6,563 ft, ~4.5 mi), then continue cross-country along the open ridge to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley Peak.

approach.expect: There is no US road to Hozomeen. From the Trans-Canada Highway (BC Hwy 1) take Exit 168 at Hope, British Columbia, follow Flood-Hope Road onto Silver-Skagit Road, and drive roughly 34 miles / 55 km of gravel south through Skagit Valley Provincial Park to the Skyline II trailhead — about an hour and a quarter. Verify the border gate status first: NPS currently prohibits both vehicle and foot traffic across the boundary at Hozomeen. From Skyline II, climb the trail roughly 8 miles and 4,000 ft to the Hozomeen Ridge junction, then turn south on the Hozomeen Ridge Trail over rolling terrain to a camp near the Monument 74 high point at about 6,345 ft, 10.5 miles in. Take water from the three creeks in the forest below Hozomeen Ridge — there is no running water again until you are south of the border. From camp the climb begins by dropping about 545 ft to the 5,800 ft saddle at the head of the north cirque. A shorter but much nastier alternative starts at the Hozomeen ranger station, follows the short Trail of the Obelisk loop, then bushwhacks east up the overgrown border swath past a swamp and gains about 3,000 ft to a col near 6,300 ft before joining the ridge; it saves miles and costs hours.

wa_hozomeen_mountain_northeast_buttress.why: Border still closed (NPS page 14 Sep 2026); approach drives Silver-Skagit Road to Skyline II, which is itself closed at km 6, so the verify-first sentence now names both.

approach.expect: A two-stage approach and the second stage is the part that stops people. Day one is a long haul of 11-plus miles under heavy loads from the road to a camp just north of the peak - the same Hozomeen Ridge / border-swath ground used by the north-side scrambling routes, reached from Silver-Skagit Road out of Hope, B.C. From that camp the approach to the base took the first ascent party a tedious and painstaking 4.5 hours: downclimb a loose third-class gully, which the party described as dangerous but the lesser of the two evils, then cross several precipitous rocky ribs and steep, unstable ground to traverse into the launch point below the wall. Budget the base approach as a half-day objective in its own right and do it in daylight. Confirm the NPS border-gate status before planning; the crossing at Hozomeen is currently closed to vehicles and foot traffic.

approach.expect: Same as the East Route to Lyman Lake/Cloudy Pass — via the currently-closed Lucerne/Holden Village/Railroad Creek trail from the east, or via the open Phelps Creek/Spider Gap trail from the west. From Lyman Lake or Cloudy Pass, gain the ridge crest at Cloudy Pass (6,440 ft) to start the traverse.
approach.value: Same as the East Route to Lyman Lake/Cloudy Pass — via the Lucerne/Holden Village/Railroad Creek trail from the east, cut off since January 28, 2026 by the Forest Service closure of the Lucerne dock and FR 8301 (order 06-17-05-26-04, through December 31, 2027), or via the Phelps Creek/Spider Gap trail from the west, whose Phelps Creek Trail #1511 is closed by the Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40, September 3 through October 31, 2026) and whose road, FR 6200, has been closed past Atkinson Flat since May 20, 2026 (order 06-17-07-2026-11, through December 31, 2027). From Lyman Lake or Cloudy Pass, gain the ridge crest at Cloudy Pass (6,440 ft) to start the traverse.

wa_north_star_mountain_cloudy_peak_trave.why: East: Lucerne dock + FR 8301 closed, order 06-17-05-26-04, 28 Jan 2026-31 Dec 2027. West was called "open": Phelps Creek Tr. 1511 is on the Little Giant Fire closure (06-17-07-2026-40, 3 Sep-31 Oct 2026) and FR 6200 is closed past Atkinson Flat (06-17-07-2026-11, 20 May 2026-31 Dec 2027) — this row's own access.closures already says the latter.
